docs.title: go-browserhttp
docs.text:
A pure-Go http.Client with a Chrome TLS fingerprint (uTLS) — bypass anti-bot 403s, no host web view.

go-browserhttp is a pure-Go, CGO_ENABLED=0 http.Client that presents a real Chrome TLS fingerprint via uTLS. Many sites 403 non-browser clients based largely on the TLS ClientHello; mimicking Chrome's ciphers, extensions and curves — plus a browser User-Agent and a warmed cookie jar — lets a plain Go client reach public endpoints with no host web view. Identical on macOS, Linux and Windows.

docs.title: browsergit
docs.text:
The git layer shared by the go-tex, go-slides and notebook playgrounds: load a project from GitHub, GitLab or Gitea/Forgejo and propose changes back as a new branch plus a pull request. Pure Go, runs in the browser (js/wasm).

Released as v0.1.0. CGO=0, BSD-3-Clause.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: Package What it is remote The Remote interface (Load, Propose, Refresh), Base, path/branch/repository validation, size limits, and Git, a Remote over git smart HTTP. forge Remote over the REST APIs of GitHub, GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo. secret Token: a credential that prints as [redacted] and refuses every encoder. browsergit (root) go-git v5 in memory, smart HTTP over the browser's Fetch: clone, status, commit, pull, push, snapshot. gitrpc The JSON protocol between a page and a git web worker.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
r, _ := forge.New(forge.Config{Kind: forge.GitHub, API: "https://api.github.com", Token: secret.New(tok)})
files, base, _ := r.Load(ctx, "owner/repo", "", "slides")
files["deck.md"] = edited
res, _ := r.Propose(ctx, base, files, remote.Proposal{
    Branch: remote.BranchName("slides/", "Fix intro", time.Now()),
    Title:  "Fix intro",
})
// res.URL is the pull request

docs.title: Reaching a forge
docs.text:
Forge Use Token GitHub forge.GitHub (REST) Fine-grained PAT: Metadata read, Contents read/write, Pull requests write. GitLab forge.GitLab (REST) OAuth (PKCE) or PAT with api scope. Gitea / Forgejo forge.Gitea (REST) when the instance allows CORS; otherwise remote.Git through a CORS proxy Access token with write:repository.

remote.Git cannot open a pull request: it pushes the new branch and returns the forge's compare page.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The token is never printed, serialised, redirected or echoed.
  • Redirects are refused, browser requests carry no cookies, and API and web bases must be https.
  • Paths and links from a server are validated; blob content must hash to its git id; sizes are bounded.
  • A proposal always creates a new branch; it never writes an existing, loaded or default branch.

Warning

A CORS proxy sees the Authorization header of every request through it, so its operator can read tokens. Prefer the REST paths (no proxy) or a proxy you run yourself. See gitcorsproxy.

docs.title: browserhttp
docs.text:
Pure-Go http.Client presenting a Chrome TLS fingerprint via uTLS. CGO=0.

A drop-in http.Client whose TLS ClientHello matches a real Chrome build, so endpoints that gate on the TLS fingerprint let it through. It pairs the uTLS handshake with a browser User-Agent and a warmed cookie jar.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• CGO_ENABLED=0, no host web view and no headless browser.
  • Real Chrome TLS fingerprint (ciphers, extensions, curves) via uTLS.
  • Browser User-Agent and a warmed cookie jar out of the box.
  • Identical behaviour on macOS, Linux and Windows.
  • Extracted from go-news-reader/reader; reusable by any browser-shaped fetcher.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
c := browserhttp.NewClient(30 * time.Second)
resp, err := c.Get("https://www.reddit.com/r/golang/hot.json")

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
go get github.com/go-browserhttp/browserhttp

Requires Go 1.26 or newer.

docs.title: gitcorsproxy
docs.text:
A CORS reverse proxy for git smart-HTTP, so a Go/wasm git client in a browser can reach remotes that speak the protocol correctly but send no Access-Control-Allow-Origin (GitHub, a bare Forgejo). Standard library only, CGO=0.

It stores nothing: the browser holds the user's token and sends it on each request; the proxy relays it upstream and forgets it.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoes the request Origin only if it is in the configured list, never *.
  • Only allow-listed upstream hosts are reachable; resolved IPs in private, loopback, link-local or metadata ranges are refused.
  • Per-client-IP rate limit, response-size cap and per-request timeout.

docs.title: Authorization handling (v0.4.0)
docs.text:
• A response to a request that carried Authorization is Cache-Control: private, no-store with Vary: Authorization, whatever the upstream said.
  • The Authorization header is never logged, query string included.
  • It is never followed through a redirect: the proxy never follows one and relays no Location.

docs.title: Hardening (v0.5.0)
docs.text:
• A refused host segment (which may be user:token@host) is logged only as a strict, bounded hostname[:port] with the userinfo dropped, otherwise as <invalid-host>.
  • -trusted-hops defaults to auto: 1 behind a reverse proxy, 0 when the proxy serves TLS itself (-tls-cert and -tls-key), where a client could otherwise choose its own X-Forwarded-For address. A non-zero value with TLS prints a warning.
  • The host is resolved once; the connection goes to the IP that was checked, and private, loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified and metadata addresses are refused at dial time (no DNS rebinding). The default transport ignores HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY.
  • Repository paths with empty, . or .. segments (also percent-encoded), control characters or backslashes, and info/refs queries without exactly one service value, are refused 400. The route parser is fuzzed.

Warning

The operator of a proxy can read every token that passes through it. Using a public proxy means trusting its operator. Prefer a forge REST API, which needs no proxy (see browsergit), or run your own proxy.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
go run ./cmd/gitcorsproxy -origins https://go-tex.github.io -hosts github.com

-origins and -hosts are required; each flag has a GITCORSPROXY_* environment variable.
